method: Feature tracing and narrow function-address inspection using the requested REAP prompts; no whole-library Ghidra import.
wrapper_rule: GNU objdump receives explicit --start-address and --stop-address bounds. Windows are selected excerpts, not complete function decompilation.
confirmed_source_facts: Same-dtype CPU-to-resident copy is accepted by custom_ops/copy_from.py and delegated to native memory.copy.
The standard copy wrapper invokes run_blocking on the returned native program.
The SDK distinguishes host sequencing copies from host-bridged dtype or device-copy cases.
HAL copy and Sequencer expose rectangular host/DRAM access; lower TP composition requires explicit chip/layout handling.
The production change uses standard copy_ rather than a new HAL or raw-pointer implementation.
limitations: Selected native bindings establish entry-point identity, not full internal copy semantics.
Native strided-copy efficiency and source-offset behavior require actual device probes.
No physical DMA byte count, raw byte-offset update API, pinned staging, or new SDK2026.3 guarantee is established.
The REA wrapper windows may end inside an instruction; no complete-function semantic proof is claimed.
